links.comparator_used: Image only ('only visual') input with no added clinical context
links.effect: Accuracy 12% with visual only vs 58% with imaging findings and clinical presentation (P < 0.001)
links.quote: With the "only visual" input format, browser-based GPT-5 achieved a diagnostic accuracy of 12%, increasing to 58% when imaging findings and clinical presentations were provided (P < 0.001).

links.comparator_used: Junior radiologists reading the same cases without GPT-5 assistance (washout between reads)
links.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy and differential diagnosis scores
links.effect: Accuracy 73% and 71% unassisted vs 87% and 86% with browser-based GPT-5 and 94% with optimal-settings GPT-5; median differential diagnosis score 4 (range 3-5) unassisted vs 5 (range 4-5) with optimal-settings GPT-5
links.quote: The radiologists' diagnostic accuracy increased from 73% and 71% without assistance to 87% and 86% with browser-based GPT-5 assistance and further to 94% with GPT-5 with optimal settings assistance.

links.comparator_used: GPT-5 using the "only visual" input format
links.outcome: GPT-5 diagnostic accuracy in abdominal cases
links.effect: 12% with "only visual" input, increasing to 58% when imaging findings and clinical presentations were provided (P < 0.001).
links.quote: With the "only visual" input format, browser-based GPT-5 achieved a diagnostic accuracy of 12%, increasing to 58% when imaging findings and clinical presentations were provided (P < 0.001).
